note: Curated tube routes for the peristalsis profile. Each route names the anatomical structures at its two ends INSTEAD of coordinates, so the ordering is justified by the atlas's own neighbouring meshes and the taught sequence rather than by a hand-typed point. 'far' means the topologically opposite end of the same mesh, used where the neighbouring structure is not in the model at all. sourceRefs carry the direction-and-mechanism claim; wave rate, width and depth are display parameters and are NOT claimed from any source.

organs.claim: A peristaltic wave carries a swallowed bolus down the oesophagus from the pharynx to the stomach.

sourceRefs.quote: The Esophagus A hollow muscular tube Conveys solid food and liquids to the stomach
Transition from voluntary to involuntary stages of swallowing as food passes downwards

organs.claim: Peristalsis moves the contents of the digestive tract onward, mouth to anus; the duodenum receives from the stomach and passes to the jejunum.

sourceRefs.quote: From mouth To anus Contraction of circular muscles behind bolus
Peristalsis Consists of waves of muscular contractions Moves a bolus along the length of the digestive tract
